Physicians are not always meeting the needs of family caregivers of the frail elderly due to various reasons, including:

* Lack of interest in helping caregivers; even if they were receptive to counseling sessions, they might be poorly remunerated for the types of counseling that are usual for caregivers.
* Limited awareness of the costs of medical care among family doctors in British Columbia.

While family physicians have some knowledge about the needs of elderly cancer patients, such as informational and relational needs similar to those of younger patients, most flagged up the need for higher levels of satisfaction, especially concerning a better dialogue with health staff and having access to people who share their same illness.
